C-APPLY-VERB.Summary: Add a top-level ngrace apply verb that is the sanctioned writer of approved to applied and of the archive move: surgical status writes on the active spec and on plan.xml (required), a fingerprint of each file's bytes after those writes, two append-only Decision records with gate applied, and a same-filesystem directory rename into archive/. The verb is not a gate subcommand. It reads permitting apply and archive Decisions from the ledger and does not re-evaluate those gates. gate apply, archive, and verdict still do not write status and never move a bundle. Partial failure rolls bytes and ledger writes back. A forced permit records itself as forced with an operator-supplied reason. This bundle's own close runs the verb.

Decided here: the verb reads the ledger and does not re-evaluate. Preconditions, all checked before any write: argv token change is a well-formed C-*; source is a directory under active/ and not under archive/; dest archive/C-* does not already exist; spec.xml exists; plan.xml exists (required; change.applied-plan-missing is why, and this is what the supersede precedent does not require); root status on spec and plan is approved, or the resume case below; opening-tag status is locatable as either quote style; hasPermittingDecision for apply is permit; hasPermittingDecision for archive is permit. Decided here: atomicity reuses supersede's write-then-rename with rollback and adds a required plan plus ledger records. Validate, write nothing. Compute next bytes in memory (status applied; surgical opening-tag attribute only, both quote styles, preserving the quote character). writeFileSync spec, then plan. Hash both on-disk files. Append two Decision records. renameSync the directory from active/ to archive/. On throw after the first artifact write, restore original file bytes and, if a Decision was appended, restore the ledger's prior bytes, while the directory is still under active/, and exit nonzero.
